To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of embedded questions did not aid the comprehension of advanced L2 learners.

(a) textual enhancement adjuncts did not aid L2 readers in comprehension; (b) L2 reading comprehension was positively related to prior subject knowledge and to L1 reading comprehension, (c) the use of textual enhancement adjunct did not compensate for the lack of prior subject knowledge, and (d) L2 reading proficiency was not related to comprehension.

embedded questions did no help L2 readers comprehend better, the effect of embedded questions was not moderated by the learners' L1 reading ability or L2 proficiency, nor by prior subject matter knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
L2 reading comprehension in the area of science and technology.
the effects of textual adjuncts, L1 reading ability and prior subject knowledge on L2 reading comprehension of advanced learners.
how L2 readers comprehend scientific passages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
textual enhancement adjuncts are not effective for advanced L2 readers.
the effects of textual enhancements are not moderated by prior subject knowledge, L2 reading ability and L2 overall proficiency.
the effect of embedded questions is moderated by the L2 proficiency of the reader, but not by prior subject knowledge, L1 reading comprehension ability, nor by the type of text adjunct.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
embedded questions do not assist L2 learners in reading comprehension.
, for advanced L2 learners in the sciences, embedded questions did not help them comprehend better.

, with advanced learners of Spanish as a foreign language, textual adjuncts did not improve comprehension, and that L1 reading ability and subject knowledge were positively correlated with L2 reading comprehension, but that textual enhancements did not aid comprehension for learners who lacked these skills.
The main takeaway from our work is that
embedded questions do not help L2 readers to better comprehend texts in L2.
L2 readers should not be expected to rely solely on the text and its embedded questions for comprehension.
L2 learners should be encouraged to read scientific texts in their L2.
